overview: Two mechanisms of horizontal gene transfer in bacteria, distinguished by whether a bacteriophage acts as the vehicle for DNA.
genZNote: Transduction: a virus is the delivery truck. Conjugation: bacteria shake hands and pass the package directly.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Transfer of bacterial DNA from one bacterium to another via a bacteriophage (virus) vector.
aspects.valueB: Direct transfer of DNA between bacteria through a physical mating bridge (pilus).

aspects.label: Transfer Vehicle
aspects.valueA: A bacteriophage capsid mistakenly packages host DNA instead of (or with) viral DNA.
aspects.valueB: A conjugative plasmid drives formation of a pilus that directly connects donor and recipient.

aspects.label: Cell-to-Cell Contact
aspects.valueA: Not required — the phage acts as an intermediary carrier between cells.
aspects.valueB: Required — direct physical connection via the sex pilus.

aspects.label: Subtypes
aspects.valueA: Generalized transduction (random DNA packaged during the lytic cycle) and specialized transduction (adjacent DNA excised with a prophage).
aspects.valueB: F+ x F- (plasmid transfer) or Hfr x F- (chromosomal gene transfer via an integrated F plasmid).

aspects.label: Clinical/Research Relevance
aspects.valueA: A route for spreading toxin genes (e.g. diphtheria toxin, some Shiga toxins) via lysogenic phages.
aspects.valueB: A major route for spreading antibiotic resistance genes among bacterial populations.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: DNA transfer mediated by a bacteriophage vector.
aspects.valueB: DNA transfer via direct physical cell-to-cell connection.
